plan: 1 Kings 2:1-9; 2 Samuel 23:1-7; 1 Kings 2:10-12; 1 Chronicles 29:26-30; Psalm 4:1-8; Psalm 5:1-12; Psalm 6:1-10; Psalm 8:1-9; Psalm 9:1-20; Psalm 11:1-7

readings.title: Daviḏ's Charge of Emunah
readings.subtitle: Guarding the Torah for Continental Authority
readings.text:
[1 Kings 2:1] And the days of Daviḏ drew near to die, and he commanded <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh his son, saying,
[2] “I am going the way of all the earth. And you shall be strong, and be a man.
[3] “And guard <dn>את</dn> the Charge of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>: to walk in <dn>His</dn> ways, to guard <dn>His</dn> laws, <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> commands, <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> right-rulings, and <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> witnesses, as it is written in the Torah of Mosheh, so that you do wisely <dn>את</dn> all that you do and <dn>את</dn> wherever you turn;
[4] so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> word which <dn>He</dn> spoke concerning me, saying, <dq>‘If your sons guard <dn>את</dn> their way, to walk before <dn>Me</dn> in truth with all their heart and with all their being,’</dq> saying, <dq>‘there is not to cease a man of yours on the throne of Yisra’ĕl.’</dq>

readings.title: Reconciling the Scales of Ra
readings.subtitle: Wisdom in Administering Retribution
readings.text:
[5] “And also, you know <dn>את</dn> what Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah did to me, and what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Yisra’ĕl, to Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr and Amasa son of Yether, that he killed them, and shed the blood of battle in peace, and put the blood of battle on his belt that was around his waist, and on his sandals that were on his feet.
[6] “So act according to your wisdom, and do not let his grey hair go down to She’ol in peace.
[7] “But show loving-commitment to the sons of Barzillai the Gil‘aḏite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for so they came to me when I fled from Aḇshalom your brother.
[8] “And see, with you is Shim‘i son of Gĕra, the Binyamite from Baḥurim, who cursed me with a grievous cursing in the day when I went to Maḥanayim. But he came down to meet me at the Yardĕn, and I swore to him by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, ‘I shall not put you to death with the sword.’
[9] “And now, do not leave him unpunished, for you are a wise man and know <dn>את</dn> what you should do to him, and shall bring <dn>את</dn> his grey hair down to She’ol with blood.”

readings.title: The Physics of a Righteous Ruler
readings.subtitle: Operating in the Fear of Elohim
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 23:1] And these are the last words of Daviḏ, the saying of Daviḏ son of Yishai, the saying of the man raised above, the anointed of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‘aqoḇ, and the sweet singer of Yisra’ĕl:
[2] “The Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken through me, And <dn>His</dn> word is on my tongue.
[3] “The <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl said, The Rock of Yisra’ĕl spoke to me, <dq>‘One who rules over man righteously,</dq>
[4] <dq>“Who rules in the fear of <dn>Elohim</dn>, Is like the light of the morning when the sun rises, A morning without clouds, Tender grass from the earth From sunshine, from rain.’</dq>

readings.title: The Everlasting Covenant
readings.subtitle: The Branch and the Eradication of Systemic Disharmony
readings.text:
[5] “For is not my house so with <dn>Ĕl</dn>? For <dn>He</dn> has made an everlasting covenant with me, Ordered in all matters, and guarded. For all my deliverance and all desire, Shall <dn>He</dn> not make it send forth a Branch?
[6] “But the worthless are all as thorns thrust away, For they are not taken with hands,
[7] “But the man who touches them Uses iron or the shaft of a spear, And with fire they are burned up in their place.”

readings.title: Daviḏ Rests with His Fathers
readings.subtitle: The Kingdom Firmly Established
readings.text:
[1 Kings 2:10] And Daviḏ slept with his fathers, and was buried in the City of Daviḏ.
[11] And the days that Daviḏ reigned over Yisra’ĕl was forty years. He reigned seven years in Ḥeḇron, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years.
[12] And Shelomoh sat on the throne of his father Daviḏ. And his reign was firmly established.

readings.title: The Totality of Daviḏ's Reign
readings.subtitle: Riches, Esteem, and the Written Witnesses
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 29:26] Thus Daviḏ son of Yishai reigned over all Yisra’ĕl.
[27] And the days that he reigned over Yisra’ĕl was forty years. He reigned seven years in Ḥeḇron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Yerushalayim.
[28] And he died in a good old age, satisfied with days, riches and esteem. And Shelomoh his son reigned in his place.
[29] And the acts of Sovereign Daviḏ, first and last, see, they are written in the book of Shemu’ĕl the seer, in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gaḏ the seer,
[30] with all his reign and his might, and the times that passed over him, and over Yisra’ĕl, and over all the reigns of the lands.

readings.title: The Elohim of My Righteousness
readings.subtitle: Separation of the Lovingly-Committed
readings.text:
[Psalm 4:1] Answer me when I call, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of my righteousness! <dn>You</dn> gave relief to me when I was in distress; Show favour to me, and hear my prayer.
[2] Till when, O you sons of men, Would you turn my esteem to shame, Would you love emptiness, seek falsehood? Selah.
[3] But know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has separated a lovingly-committed one for <dn>Himself</dn>; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> hears when I call to <dn>Him</dn>.

readings.title: Slaughterings of Righteousness
readings.subtitle: Dwelling in Absolute Safety
readings.text:
[4] Tremble, and do not sin. Speak within your heart on your bed, and be still. Selah.
[5] Slaughter slaughterings of righteousness, And trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[6] Many are saying, “Who would show us good?” <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, lift up the light of <dn>Your</dn> face upon us.
[7] <dn>You</dn> have put more gladness in my heart, Than in the season that their grain and wine increased.
[8] I lie down in peace altogether, and sleep; For <dn>You</dn> alone, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, make me dwell in safety.

readings.title: Presenting the Morning Meditation
readings.subtitle: The Rejection of Destructive Friction
readings.text:
[Psalm 5:1] Give ear to my words, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Consider my meditation.
[2] Attend to the voice of my cry, My Sovereign and my <dn>Elohim</dn>, For unto <dn>You</dn> I pray.
[3] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in the morning <dn>You</dn> hear my voice; I present myself to <dn>You</dn> in the morning, And I look up.
[4] For <dn>You</dn> are not an <dn>Ĕl</dn> taking delight in wrong, Nor does evil dwell with <dn>You</dn>.
[5] The boasters do not stand before <dn>Your</dn> eyes; <dn>You</dn> hate all workers of wickedness.
[6] <dn>You</dn> destroy those speaking falsehood; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> loathes a man of blood and deceit.
[7] But I, I enter <dn>Your</dn> house In the greatness of <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment; I bow myself toward <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Hĕḵal in <dn>Your</dn> fear.

readings.title: Surrounded by Favour
readings.subtitle: Exulting in the Name
readings.text:
[8] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, lead me in <dn>Your</dn> righteousness because of those watching me; Make <dn>Your</dn> way straight before my face.
[9] For there is no stability in their mouth; Their inward part is destruction; Their throat is an open burial-site; They flatter with their tongue.
[10] Declare them guilty, O <dn>Elohim</dn>! Let them fall by their own counsels; Thrust them away for their many transgressions, Because they have rebelled against <dn>You</dn>.
[11] But let all who take refuge in <dn>You</dn> rejoice; Let them ever shout for joy, because <dn>You</dn> shelter them; And let those who love <dn>Your</dn> Name exult in <dn>You</dn>.
[12] For <dn>You</dn> bless the righteous, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; <dn>You</dn> surround him with favour as with a shield.

readings.title: Pleading for the Premial Reward
readings.subtitle: Healing the Exhausted Vessel
readings.text:
[Psalm 6:1] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do not rebuke me in <dn>Your</dn> displeasure, Nor discipline me in <dn>Your</dn> wrath.
[2] Show favour to me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for I am fading away; O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, heal me, for my bones have been troubled.
[3] And my being has been greatly troubled; And <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – till when?
[4] Return, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, rescue my life! Oh, save me for <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment’ sake!
[5] For in death there is no remembrance of <dn>You</dn>; Who gives <dn>You</dn> thanks in She’ol?

readings.title: The Voice of Weeping Heard
readings.subtitle: The Sudden Reversal of the Adversary
readings.text:
[6] I have grown weary with my groaning; Every night I flood my bed; I drench my couch with my tears.
[7] My eye has grown dim because of grief; It grows old because of all my adversaries.
[8] Depart from me, all you workers of wickedness; For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has heard the voice of my weeping.
[9] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has heard my pleading; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> receives my prayer.
[10] Let all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled; They turn back suddenly, ashamed.

readings.title: The Architecture of the Heavens
readings.subtitle: The Composite Whole and the Son of Man
readings.text:
[Psalm 8:1] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, our Master, how excellent is <dn>Your</dn> Name in all the earth, <dn>You</dn> who set <dn>Your</dn> splendour above the heavens!
[2] Out of the mouth of babes and infants <dn>You</dn> have founded strength, Because of <dn>Your</dn> adversaries, To put an end to enemy and avenger.
[3] For I see <dn>Your</dn> heavens, the work of <dn>Your</dn> fingers, The moon and the stars, which <dn>You</dn> have established.
[4] What is man that <dn>You</dn> remember him? And the son of man that <dn>You</dn> visit him?
[5] Yet <dn>You</dn> have made him a little less than <dn>Elohim</dn>, And have crowned him with esteem and splendour.

readings.title: Dominion Over the Works
readings.subtitle: The Excellent Name in All the Earth
readings.text:
[6] <dn>You</dn> made him rule over the works of <dn>Your</dn> hands; <dn>You</dn> have put all under his feet,
[7] All sheep and oxen, And also the beasts of the field,
[8] The birds of the heavens, And the fish of the sea, Passing through the paths of the seas.
[9] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, our Master, How excellent is <dn>Your</dn> Name in all the earth!

readings.title: The Throne of Righteousness
readings.subtitle: The Eradication of Systemic Confusion
readings.text:
[Psalm 9:1] Aleph I praise <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with all my heart; I declare all <dn>Your</dn> wonders.
[2] I rejoice and exult in <dn>You</dn>; I sing praise to <dn>Your</dn> Name, O Most High.
[3] Bĕt When my enemies turn back, They stumble and perish before <dn>You</dn>.
[4] For <dn>You</dn> executed my right and my cause, <dn>You</dn> sat on the throne judging in righteousness.
[5] Gimel <dn>You</dn> have rebuked the nations, <dn>You</dn> have destroyed the wrong, <dn>You</dn> have wiped out their name forever and ever.
[6] Hĕ The enemy is no more – ruins everlasting! And <dn>You</dn> have uprooted the cities; Even their remembrance has perished.

readings.title: Judging the World in Straightness
readings.subtitle: Trusting the Character of the Name
readings.text:
[7] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> abides forever, <dn>He</dn> is preparing <dn>His</dn> throne for judgment.
[8] And <dn>He</dn> judges the world in righteousness, <dn>He</dn> judges the peoples in straightness.
[9] Waw And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a refuge for the crushed one, A refuge in times of distress.
[10] And those who know <dn>Your</dn> Name trust in <dn>You</dn>, For <dn>You</dn> have not forsaken those who seek <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[Psalm 9:11] Zayin Sing praises to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who dwells in Tsiyon! Declare <dn>His</dn> deeds among the peoples.
[12] For <dn>He</dn> remembers the seekers of bloodshed, <dn>He</dn> does not forget the cry of the afflicted.

readings.title: The Nations Snared in Their Own Works
readings.subtitle: The Expectancy of the Poor
readings.text:
[13] Ḥet Show favour to me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! See my affliction by those who hate me, <dn>You</dn> who lift me up from the gates of death,
[14] So that I declare all <dn>Your</dn> praise In the gates of the daughter of Tsiyon. I rejoice in <dn>Your</dn> deliverance.
[15] Tet The nations have sunk down in the pit which they made; In the net which they hid, their own foot is caught.
[16] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made <dn>Himself</dn> known, <dn>He</dn> has done right-ruling; The wrong is snared in the work of his own hands. Meditation. Selah.
[17] Yod The wrong return to She’ol, All the nations that forget <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[18] Kaph For the needy is not always forgotten; Neither the expectancy of the poor lost forever.
[19] Arise, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Do not let man prevail; Let the nations be judged before <dn>Your</dn> face.
[20] Put them in fear, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Let the nations know they are but men. Selah.

readings.title: When the Foundations are Destroyed
readings.subtitle: Taking Refuge in the Set-Apart One
readings.text:
[Psalm 11:1] In <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> I have taken refuge; Why do you say to me, “Flee to your mountain like a bird”?
[2] For look! The wrong bend a bow, They set their arrow on the string, To shoot in darkness at the upright in heart.
[3] When the foundations are destroyed, What shall the righteous do?

readings.title: The Eyes That Examine
readings.subtitle: The Upright Shall See His Face
readings.text:
[4] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is in <dn>His</dn> set-apart Hĕḵal, The throne of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is in the heavens. <dn>His</dn> eyes see, <dn>His</dn> eyelids examine the sons of men.
[5] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> tries the righteous, But <dn>His</dn> being shall hate the wrong And the one who loves violence.
[6] Upon the wrong <dn>He</dn> rains snares, Fire and sulphur and a scorching wind Are the portion of their cup.
[7] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is righteous, <dn>He</dn> has loved righteousness; The upright shall see <dn>His</dn> face.
